title: Commitment discount smoothing and timezone-aware export reconciler
creator: Rafael Ortega
description: Some customers on Reserved/Dedicated capacity have seen invoice mismatches when commitment discounts are split across local billing boundaries (DST transitions, customer timezone-aligned billing windows). Our existing hourly-anchored export produces discount line items that are attributed to the wrong invoice boundary in NetSuite/Stripe, causing customer confusion and manual reconciliation. This ticket implements a timezone-aware normalization step and a smoothing/amortization algorithm in the export reconciler so commitment discounts are allocated deterministically across split windows and exports are idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: Exports normalize customer billing windows to a UTC-anchored canonical window and record the original local window in metadata
Commitment discounts that cross a billing boundary are amortized into deterministic line items whose sum matches the expected committed total for the invoice period
Generated export files include an immutable export signature and checksum to support idempotent replays
Reconciler test harness flags any invoice delta > $25 or >0.2% for automated review
No regressions in existing billing exports (existing nightly export job passes conformance suite)
technical_notes: Add a normalization layer: convert customer-defined billing windows into canonical UTC windows anchored at customer's billing start-of-day offset
Smoothing algorithm: fractional allocation per sub-hour bucket, preserve cent-level rounding invariant by applying largest-residual-first distribution
Export format change: add fields export_window_start_utc, original_window_zone, export_checksum, export_version
Idempotency: include deterministic export_id computed from (customer_id, window_start_utc, export_version) and sign with billing-worker key
Backfill strategy: for historical windows with >$250 anomaly, mark for manual backfill rather than automated patching to preserve audit trail
testing_plan: Unit tests for timezone normalization across DST boundaries (US, EU, APAC test vectors)
Property-based tests for amortization algorithm to prove sum invariants across random window splits
Integration test: run export job against sandbox NetSuite connector validating line item mapping and invoice totals
Load test: simulate 10k customers concurrently exporting to ensure export job latency stays within SLA
Canary: enable reconciler for 5% of customers for 48 hours and compare anomaly rates vs baseline
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch behind feature flag 'discount_smoothing_v1'
Run canary for 5% of customers in staging and then prod for 48h
Monitor anomaly dashboard and run automated rollback if anomaly_rate > 0.5% or error_rate increases
Gradually increase rollout to 25% -> 75% -> 100% over 7 days
Post-rollout: run a reconciliation sweep to surface historical windows needing manual review
